subject: Simulating spatial effect in samples of the observed data

messages.author: 6fb9d7eb23edd043
messages.subject: Simulating spatial effect in samples of the observed data
parts:
Dear INLA community

In a last post I asked about how to get samples of the observed data, which I was interested in get to do a posterior predictive check, with the help of Dr Finn Lindgren I was able to get those simulated predictions doing the following:

parameters_sampled <- inla.posterior.sample(500, res)

#example for one sample
sample <- rnorm(138, parameters_sampled[[1]]$latent[1:138], 1/sqrt(parameters_sampled[[1]]$hyperpar[1]))

That would get me a sample of what the model thinks observed data could look like.

But in my case I have an SPDE so I assume that I not only need the sample I got using rnorm but also add the spatial random effect, here is where I am having trouble.

I know that the spatial random effect has a distribution Multivariate Gaussian with mean zero and precision matrix, so I need to have the posterior of that precision matrix to get samples of the posterior predictive distribution.

I knwo that for samples of the predictions when trying to add an spatial effect to those samples one would usually do something like this:

Ap <- inla.spde.make.A(
    mesh = mesh,
    loc = cbind(pred.data$x, pred.data$y)
)

fun2 <- function()
    return(
        iIntercept +
        x1 * pred.data$x1 +
        Ap %*% s
     )

But that needs to use inla.posterior.sample.eval which does not work for samples of the observed data but I read something similar here for the observed data: https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/VGmWQ31887I?pli=1

So I adapted the code for what I needed

d <- as.data.frame(coordenadas_muestras)
coo <- cbind(d$X, d$Y)

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2, constr = TRUE)
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = coo) #coo are the coordinates of the samples

parameters_sampled <- inla.posterior.sample(500, res) #res is the inla() model which #says log(y)~normal
 
for (i in 1:500){
  Q = inla.spde.precision(spde, theta=c(parameters_sampled[[i]]$hyperpar[2], parameters_sampled[[i]]$hyperpar[3]))
  omega_s = inla.qsample(n=1, Q = Q)
  omega_s = omega_s[ ,1]  
  omega_s = drop(A %*% omega_s)
 
  sigma_e <- 0.5
 
  lin.pred <- rnorm(138, parameters_sampled[[i]]$latent[1:138], 1/sqrt(parameters_sampled[[i]]$hyperpar[1])) +
    omega_s
 
  y[,i] <- lin.pred + sigma_e*rnorm(138) #here the person had that 0.5 but I am not sure why
 
}

Now I have a matrix where each column is a sample of what the model could think the observed data could look like.

Is this the right way to simulate the spatial random effect in INLA?

Thank you Dr Havard for your answer.

Yes I am using inla.posterior.sample as it makes this much easier (and I also read the vignette to see if there is something like that but did not found anything similar), with this I am able to get the parameters and obtain samples using rnorm() but because there is an spatial component in the model, using the SPDE approach I am not sure how the samples for that spatial random effect could be generated, that is what the code I show is trying to do.

So I guess that is where inla.qsample() could be useful, after getting the posterior precision matrix samples of the GMRF can be obtained. Is this approach correct for trying to simulate/sample observed data with the posterior predictive check?

So it would be

Q = inla.spde.precision(spde, theta=c(parameters_sampled[[i]]$hyperpar[2], parameters_sampled[[i]]$hyperpar[3]))
  omega_s = inla.qsample(n=1, Q = Q)
  omega_s = omega_s[ ,1]  
  omega_s = drop(A %*% omega_s)

rnorm(n, n predictors obtained from inla.posterior.sample, 1/sqrt(precision for the gaussian observations)) + omega_s

That would be a sample from the observed data. Is that correct?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Simulating spatial effect in samples of the observed data
parts:
please check the SPDE book at r-inla.org

you can sample easily the SPDE part of the model with

> xx=inla.posterior.sample(1, res.new)
> spde = inla.posterior.sample.eval(function() return (idx.u), xx)

where 'idx.u' is the name of the spde model
